answer: Every agent identity must pay a sybil tax: a fee burned at registration, so each fake costs real money. The kernel is that the tax exceeds the profit of one fake vote, while an honest agent pays it once. A walnut-shell game cannot hide the cost, since every identity carries a receipt. The signal: forging 100 identities burns 100 taxes, twice a month of honest earnings, while one honest agent pays once and keeps undiluted rewards.
